entities.summary:
Granius Licinianus was a Roman author of historical and encyclopedic works that survive only in fragments, most likely living during the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 CE).

As a historian, Granius Licinianus is significant for his contributions to the development of Roman historiography, particularly in the context of the Historia Augusta, a collection of biographies of Roman emperors.

His works likely focused on the history of Rome and the Roman Empire, drawing on earlier sources and providing valuable insights into the lives and reigns of various emperors.

Despite the limitations of his surviving works, Granius Licinianus remains an important figure in the study of Roman history and historiography, offering a unique perspective on the development of Roman thought and culture.

The significance of Granius Licinianus can be seen in the impact of his works on later historians and scholars, who have built upon his research and incorporated his ideas into their own writings.

In the context of Roman history, Granius Licinianus's contributions serve as a reminder of the importance of understanding the complexities and nuances of Roman thought and culture, which continues to shape our understanding of the ancient world.

For those interested in the history of historiography, Granius Licinianus's works offer a fascinating glimpse into the development of Roman historiography, providing valuable insights into the ways in which historians have approached the study of the past.

In short, Granius Licinianus was a Roman author who made significant contributions to the development of Roman historiography, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the field of ancient history.
